title: Lost in Translation: How Universal Ethical Values Fail to Translate Across Global Contexts
abstract: arXiv:2608.20490v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: AI ethics frameworks treat values such as fairness, transparency, and accountability as universal and uniformly operationalizable across contexts. We examined how 14 experts across 10 countries made sense of AI in practice, reinterpreted core values, and envisioned governance alternatives. We found that AI deployment is characterized by structurally unequal conditions, marked by infrastructural constraints, extractive practices, and a "mystification" of technology, which fundamentally shape perceptions of risks and opportunities. Our findings reveal that experts reinterpret values to fit local moral logics: privacy as collective and relational rather than individual; transparency as trust-building accountability rather than technical disclosure; and fairness as equity in access and representation rather than parity in outcomes. We identify these as translation gaps between encoded global frameworks and situated local practices. Finally,

translated_abstract: 摘要：人工智能伦理框架将公平、透明和问责等价值观视为普适的，并可在不同情境中统一实施。我们研究了来自10个国家的14位专家如何在实践中理解人工智能，重新诠释核心价值，并设想治理替代方案。我们发现，人工智能部署以结构性不平等条件为特征，表现为基础设施限制、剥削性实践和技术的“神秘化”，这些从根本上塑造了对风险和机遇的认知。我们的发现表明，专家们根据当地道德逻辑重新诠释价值：隐私被视为集体性和关系性而非个人性；透明被视为建立信任的问责机制而非技术披露；公平被视为获取和代表方面的平等而非结果上的均等。我们将这些识别为编码的全球框架与情境化本地实践之间的翻译差距。最后，
tldr: 本文揭示了全球AI伦理框架中的普世价值在本地实践中因结构性不平等和道德逻辑差异而产生翻译差距，导致价值意义被重新诠释。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that universal AI ethical values fail to translate across global contexts due to structural inequalities and local moral logics, leading to reinterpretations of core values.
